svg.text: K1. A smaller arena: a loop round a point
A great circle is the biggest loop on a planet. A loop of a smaller circle goes round a centre point instead. Planet 7, to the same scale as picture A2.
ocean

city
town
Three loops on the same planet
The great circle: 153,600 units round (today).
It goes through the middle of the planet.
A loop of 76,800 units: half as long. It circles
a centre 12,800 units away from every point of
it.
A loop of 38,400 units: a quarter as long. Its
centre is 6,177 units from the line, and the
loop is 6,111 units in radius.
What the two loops hold (planet 7)
76,800: 2 cities, 4 towns, 4 biomes, 71% land, 55% of its length settled
38,400: 1 city, 3 towns, 3 biomes, 71% land, 66% of its length settled
These are the best loop found of each size, from
loops round every city and town and some random
points. A loop meets the minimum far less often than
a great circle does (next picture), so the picker
tries more of them.
A loop can go round anything
A city, a mountain range, a lake, or a pole (K2): a
ring of ice sheet round the south pole, a ring of
sea ice round the north.
